contentHtml:
v4.7.0 is the next minor release.

📣 Some news

🧪 Try Nitro v3 today

You can now build your Nuxt 4 app with Nitro v3 (#37101). Nitro v3 is what Nuxt 5 is built on, so this is a way to move your server code (and your modules) over before you upgrade Nuxt itself.

There's no config to change. Just add nitro to your dependencies:

npm install nitro

If nitro is in your package.json, Nuxt builds with Nitro v3. To go back, just remove it.

Caution

This is highly experimental. Nitro v3 is still a release candidate, and there are no guarantees. Please try it on a branch, not in production. 🙏

Do give Nitro v3 a try! On our benchmark app with about 170 pages, the same app on 4.7 served 33% more requests per second on its home page with Nitro v3 than with Nitro v2 (926 to 1,236), and 44% more on a page with 1,000 links (219 to 316), with identical HTML.

On Nuxt 4, Nitro v3 runs with a compatibility layer, nitroLegacy, which keeps imports from h3, nitropack and #imports resolving, keeps the Nitro v2 auto-imports, useRuntimeConfig(event), event.node and the Nitro v2 hooks working, and keeps a long list of h3 v1 behaviours. Once things work, set nitroLegacy: false to find the code that still depends on it.

A few things change with Nitro v3 regardless. The main one is route rules: /blog/* now also applies to /blog/2026/hello. Nuxt warns about each rule whose meaning changes (NUXT_B4029), and stops on a rule with more than one wildcard, like /api/*/items/**, which you can rewrite with a named parameter (/api/:id/items/**). Your app matches route rules the same way as the server, so Nuxt-only rules like appMiddleware and ssr apply to the same paths on both.

The other is imports. If your server code imported a package your app didn't depend on, Nitro v2 fell back to Nuxt's own dependencies. Nitro v3 doesn't, so nuxt dev fails with something like Cannot find package 'ufo'. Make sure every package your server code imports is in your package.json. The upgrade guide has the full list.

If something breaks for you (and it might), please open an issue and mention Nitro v3. ❤️

🖥️ Nuxt CLI 4.1

Nuxt 4.7 also comes with Nuxt CLI 4.1. The most visible change is that the CLI now renders the whole production build itself, from a set of new build hooks, with every builder and server builder (thanks to @atinux, nuxt/cli#1662, #37194):

nuxt generate shows the prerendered routes in the same way, and ends by suggesting where to deploy. Logs from Nuxt and modules stay inside the build output rather than breaking out of it (nuxt/cli#1705), and with nitropack v2.14 a route that fails to prerender is listed with the pages that link to it (#37245).

There's more:

  • nuxt dev --https serves over HTTP/2 (thanks to @ProgramRipper, nuxt/cli#1694)
  • you can click and scroll inside the panes of the dev panel (thanks to @Flo0806, nuxt/cli#1665)
  • copying a URL or an error works without a system clipboard, for example over SSH or in a container (nuxt/cli#1693)
  • new nuxt module build and nuxt module prepare commands for module authors (nuxt/cli#1687), paving the way for @nuxt/module-builder v2, built on tsdown with support for TypeScript 7.1 (watch this space!)

👀 Highlights

🤖 WebMCP (experimental)

WebMCP is a proposed browser API that lets a page offer tools to AI agents running in the browser. With experimental.webmcp, tagging a function with @tool is enough (#37195):

<script setup lang="ts">
/**
 * Add one of a product to the cart. Use when the user wants to buy something.
 * @tool
 */
function addToCart (sku: string) {
  cart.value.push(sku)
}
</script>

<template>
  <button v-for="product in products" :key="product.sku" :disabled="!product.inStock" @click="addToCart(product.sku)">
    Add {{ product.name }}
  </button>
</template>

The arguments come from your template, so an agent can only do what a user could click. A @tool on a @submit handler fills in and submits the form for real, defineAgentTool() and useAgentTool() cover tools that don't map to one control, and useAgentActivity() shows the user what an agent is doing (with a way to stop it).

Nuxt also registers a navigate tool listing your pages, warns at build time about bindings that can't become tools (or descriptions that don't follow Chrome's tool design guidance), and in development writes each page's tools to .nuxt/webmcp/schema.json for webmcp-evals. In browsers without WebMCP, nothing registers and your app behaves exactly as before.

This started from @sdras's proposal for Vue and WebMCP, and much of its shape comes from her work and feedback. Thank you, Sarah! 💚

👉 Read the WebMCP guide.

🔎 All your problems in one place

With my-bad v1 and vite-plugin-checker v1, the dev error badge now collects problems too (#36918): type errors (with typescript.typeCheck), ESLint or any other Vite checker, Vue compiler warnings (#36967) and Nuxt's own scan warnings (#36969). Each opens in a drawer beside your page, or in the DevTools v4 dock.

And thanks to @sakaintp, typescript.typeCheck can now be 'dev' or 'build' (#36164).

🩺 Template diagnostics

Nuxt now checks your templates for mistakes the Vue compiler can't know about (#36754): a <NuxtLink> whose static to doesn't match any page (NUXT_B4025), and v-on, v-model, functions or class instances on a server component (NUXT_B3014, NUXT_B3015).

 WARN  [NUXT_B4025] <NuxtLink to="/abuot"> in app/pages/broken-link.vue does not match any page route.
├▶ fix: Check the path for typos or add a page for it. To link to a server route, a file in public/ or another site, set the external prop.
├▶ sources: app/pages/broken-link.vue:3:15
╰▶ see: https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/errors/b4025

In development, these also show up on every open page until you fix them. Turn them off with experimental.templateDiagnostics: false.

🧯 Server-side error boundaries

With experimental.ssrErrorBoundary (on with compatibilityVersion: 5), <NuxtErrorBoundary> catches errors during server rendering too (#36990). One broken component no longer takes down the page: you get a 200, the #error slot in its place, and the client hydrates into the same state. A new retry-on-client prop replaces <NuxtClientFallback>, which is now deprecated. The slot also exposes clearBoundaryError, the same method as clearError under a name that can't be confused with the global clearError (#37079).

✅ Validated runtime config

Any value in runtimeConfig can now be a Standard Schema (Zod, ArkType, Valibot...) (#36905):

import { z } from 'zod'

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  runtimeConfig: {
    apiSecret: z.string(), // required at runtime
    public: {
      mode: z.enum(['preview', 'production']).default('production'),
    },
  },
})

Environment variables are converted to the schema's type at startup, and if anything is missing or invalid, the server doesn't start, and you get one error listing all of it. The schema itself never ends up in your server bundle.

🚀 Performance

We spent a lot of this release profiling. On the starter app from e18e's framework benchmarks, and on our own benchmark apps:

v4.6.4 v4.7.0 installed packages, starter 523 473 -50 server output, starter 2.17 MB 1.23 MB -43% initial page load, starter 80.4 kB, 14 requests 66.3 kB, 3 requests -18% SSR throughput, starter 245 req/s 292 req/s +19% SSR throughput, a page with 1,000 <NuxtLink>s 88 req/s 218 req/s 2.5x SSR throughput, ~170 pages, with staticRoutes 890 req/s 1,976 req/s 2.2x total blocking time, Nuxt UI landing page 276 ms 180 ms -35%

Some of the work behind that:

  • a new opt-in experimental.staticRoutes builds the server's route matcher once instead of per request, if you don't add routes at runtime (#36867) 🔥
  • V8 compile hints on the entry, layout and page chunks, and yielding between boot phases, for faster hydration (#36758, #36760)
  • static internal <NuxtLink>s render as plain anchors (#36904), and rendered HTML is encoded chunk by chunk (#36719)
  • ofetch is left out of the client when nothing uses $fetch (#35790), and so is unhead when nothing on the client touches the head, even without your own error.vue (#37035, #37243)
  • the browser loads fewer files before hydration (6 instead of 18 on our Nuxt UI benchmark page)
  • with experimental.viteEnvironmentApi (or compatibilityVersion: 5), the client and server build at the same time (#37047), and nuxt.schema files, decorators and JSX only cost build time when you use them (#37027, #37053, #37054)
  • in development, a request that's still rendering when the server rebuilds finishes on the old code instead of failing with a 503 (#37245)
  • nuxt no longer depends on @nuxt/devtools, and ships the tiny @nuxt/devtools-onboard instead, which loads DevTools v3 or v4 if you have it, or offers to install it (thanks to @antfu, #36581)

nuxt build is about 7% faster on the large app and about 6% slower on the starter, and nuxt dev starts as quickly as before.

A huge thank-you to @onmax, who sent over twenty performance PRs for this release. ❤️

🦀 Rsbuild builder

Thanks to @Nsttt, there's a new @nuxt/rsbuild-builder (builder: 'rsbuild') that hands your build to Rsbuild itself (#36499). It replaces @nuxt/rspack-builder, which is now deprecated.

🧰 For module authors

  • renderer plugins (addRendererPlugin()) add to the initial HTML with any server builder (#36601), plus a new render:document hook (#36989)
  • build:environment:* and build:prerender:* hooks report every bundle and prerendered route (#37194)
  • updateRuntimeConfig() accepts schemas, and there are extendRsbuildConfig() and addRsbuildPlugin()
  • defineHandler from nuxt/server, matching Nitro v3 (thanks to @atinux, #36929)
  • a nuxt.request tracing channel for APM tools (thanks to @logaretm, #36483)

🛠️ And more

  • addRouteMiddleware returns a function to remove the middleware again (#37080)
  • onNuxtReady accepts a timeout and a signal (#36743)
  • sourcemap: { client: 'nosource' } and a finish-color prop for <NuxtLoadingIndicator> (thanks to @0xgdr, #36534, #36533)
  • navigateTo(url, { open }) can pass noopener by default, with experimental.defaults.navigateTo.noopener (on with compatibilityVersion: 5) (#37075)
  • NuxtLinkSlotProps is exported from nuxt/app (thanks to @VividLemon, #37092)
  • serverFetch is typed against your server routes (#36543)
  • with Nitro v3, Nuxt warns in development when runtime config is mutated during server rendering (NUXT_E1014, #37076)
  • when Node.js has to reparse your nuxt.config as ESM, Nuxt suggests adding "type": "module" to your package.json (#37205)

🩹 Fixes

As always, lots of fixes. To name a few: @pawell67 made callOnce rerun after navigating away while it runs and stopped Nitro creating a request body stream until it's read (#37149, #37129), @astraldev made cookies set before a streamed response starts reach the browser and kept page loading going while a page is still pending (#37131, #37165), @waleedtariq109 made lazy hydration replay the interaction that triggered it (#36838), @lafllamme made a failed read of shared prerender data retry on later routes instead of prerendering them with null (#37244), and @posva kept the browser's restored scroll position on reload (#36957).

🔒 Security

This release fixes four security issues. We recommend upgrading. The advisories have the full details (and will be released later on 24 November).

  • Route rules on _payload.json (GHSA-jxc9-w3j6-pwp2, medium): affects a wildcard cache, swr or isr rule together with a more specific rule for a page. One user's page data could be cached and served to another.
  • Encoded slashes on catch-all routes (GHSA-vrh2-cfcx-c3fg, medium): an incomplete fix for GHSA-f3x9-2chm-73c8, affecting route rules (such as appMiddleware) on a catch-all page.
  • Dev server runtime config (GHSA-h5xj-x893-p5f7, low, development only): affects nuxt dev reachable from an untrusted network.

Thank you to @inanna-malick, @stilwel, @kanokwut, @onur-yuksekkaya, @DicksonWu654 and @rexpository for reporting these responsibly. 💚

Important

If you use cache, swr or isr route rules on pages with user-specific data, purge any CDN or edge cache that may already hold a _payload.json after you upgrade.

⚠️ Heads-up

  • Nuxt DevTools is no longer installed with Nuxt. If you use it, add @nuxt/devtools to your devDependencies (or click the button nuxt dev shows you).
  • Nuxt warns when your app's vue is older than the version it needs (NUXT_B7042). Nuxt 4.7 requires vue ^3.5.46, and npx nuxt upgrade --dedupe updates it along with Nuxt.
  • Template diagnostics are on, so you may see new NUXT_B4025 warnings. For a link to a server route, a file in public/ or another site, add the external prop.
  • With experimental.viteEnvironmentApi, the client and server build in parallel. If a Vite plugin reads the client build output from the server build, set experimental.parallelBuild: false.
  • globalThis.$fetch is only installed on the client when something uses it. If you read it somewhere Nuxt can't see at build time, set experimental.globalFetch: true.
  • @nuxt/rspack-builder and <NuxtClientFallback> are deprecated, in favour of @nuxt/rsbuild-builder and <NuxtErrorBoundary retry-on-client>.

✅ Upgrading

Our recommendation for upgrading is to run:

npx nuxt upgrade --dedupe

This will refresh your lockfile and pull in the latest dependencies Nuxt relies on, including Nuxt CLI 4.1, my-bad v1 and vite-plugin-checker v1.

If you'd like to try Nitro v3, read Testing Nitro v3 in the upgrade guide first.

👉 Read the full release post for more details and examples.

We recommend upgrading as soon as you can. ⚠️ Behaviour changes These probably won't affect most apps, but it's worth flagging anyway: Error details in production. When a…
contentHtml:
4.6.4 is a security release. It fixes eight advisories in Nuxt and pulls in nitropack 2.13.6, which fixes three more in Nitro. We recommend upgrading as soon as you can.

⚠️ Behaviour changes

These probably won't affect most apps, but it's worth flagging anyway:

  1. Error details in production. When a page fails to render on the server, the error page and the payload now only carry message and data of errors you create with createError. Everything else is stripped.
  2. Dev server Host checks. Webpack and rspack dev servers now reject requests with an unexpected Host header, as Vite already does. If you use a custom hostname or tunnel, you'll need to add it to the new devServer.allowedHosts option.
  3. workspaceDir detection. When workspaceDir isn't set, Nuxt now only widens it past rootDir to an explicit workspace root or the closest git repository.
  4. Nitropack cached routes. cache, swr and isr route rules now only cache GET and HEAD requests, and no longer store responses that set a cookie or send Cache-Control: private or no-store. Wildcard proxy and redirect rules also reject requests whose resolved target would leave the rule's scope.
  5. Route rules and encoded slashes. Route rules now match paths that contain encoded slashes, so /api%2Fadmin is covered by a /api/** rule.
